\[
V_\sigma = \exp\!\left(-\frac{R_B^2}{2\beta^2}\right)\left(1 - \exp\!\left(-\frac{S^2}{2\gamma^2}\right)\right),
\qquad
R_B = \frac{\lvert\lambda_1\rvert}{\lambda_2},\quad S = \sqrt{\lambda_1^2 + \lambda_2^2},
\qquad
\beta = 0.5
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\lambda_1, \lambda_2\): The Hessian eigenvalues, |lambda_1| <= |lambda_2|
- \(R_B\): The blob ratio
- \(S\): The structure, the norm of the Hessian
- \(\beta, \gamma\): The blob and structure constants

The Hessian is the matrix of second derivatives of the image smoothed by a Gaussian of sigma. Its eigenvalues lambda_1 and lambda_2 are the curvatures along and across the strongest bend. They are sorted so that |lambda_1| <= |lambda_2|. In the middle of a dark line, the brightness bends up strongly across the line, so lambda_2 is large and positive. It hardly bends along the line, so lambda_1 is near 0. Frangi's measure is large exactly there. The ratio R_B is near 1 for round blobs, so the first factor removes them. S is large wherever there is structure at all, so the second factor removes flat noise. Where lambda_2 has the wrong sign, scikit-image clips it to 1e-10, so V is 0. The 3D plate term of the paper is 1 in 2D. The filter keeps the largest V over the scales and stretches the result so the strongest response is white.
